title: Range-Capped Sinkhorn for Reliable Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections

raw.stage1:
### Purpose:
The contribution's purpose is to diagnose why mHC's learnable routing matrices fail to learn. None of the prior papers explicitly diagnose this specific failure mode of mHC routing matrices. While [1] discusses mHC and its limitations, it does not address the specific issue of learnable routing matrices collapsing due to underflow or zero Jacobian. Similarly, [26] mentions router collapse in single-gated MoEs but does not analyze mHC or its specific failure mechanism. No prior paper establishes the same empirical relationship or failure diagnosis.

### Mechanism:
The contribution analyzes the Sinkhorn projection under specific default settings (temperature tau=0.05, off-diagonal init -8) and demonstrates that the input log-range reaches 160, causing exp(-160) underflow to zero and collapsing the output to an exact permutation matrix with zero Jacobian. [13] discusses phase transitions in the Sinkhorn-Knopp algorithm but does not analyze underflow or the specific collapse mechanism described here. [6] analyzes convergence properties of Sinkhorn-Knopp with sparse cost matrices but does not address the underflow or zero Jacobian issue. [11] discusses underflow in mixed precision training but does not analyze Sinkhorn projections or routing matrices. No prior paper contains a substantively equivalent mechanism.

### Evaluation:
The contribution evaluates the gradients of H_res under default settings, showing they are exactly 0.0 across all layers and training steps on a 48-layer GPT-2 model. This evaluation design involves measuring gradient values across layers and steps, which is a standard ablation-style analysis. Papers such as [1] and [26] evaluate mHC and MoE architectures but do not use the same evaluation design to measure gradient collapse across layers and steps. No prior paper uses this specific evaluation design.

### Domain:
The contribution operates in the domain of deep learning architecture, specifically Sinkhorn-based routing in hyper-connections. [1] and [26] both address hyper-connections and routing mechanisms in deep learning architectures, which places them in the same general application area. Although this contribution targets a specific failure mode, the domain is covered by prior work in hyper-connections and routing.
